title: Thirteen on the List
subtitle: Monday 11 to Saturday 16 April 1927: The Company Says Squeeze, the Courthouse in Gale, the Kept Light, and the Vote

setting.name: Ottway and Gale, the week after Dewey Spradlin was taken
setting.description: A man is alive behind the 7 North seal and the company will not open it; he has until midnight on Tuesday 19 April. This is the week the camp divides and the party dig up 1919: the store ledger, the tonnage sheets, the inquest file in the Gale courthouse, the fire boss's book, the Mount Moriah register, and the old lamp man who kept a light burning for seven and a half years without knowing why. The company answers with evictions, a guard on the seal, a new contract and, on Thursday night, the coke ovens banked to punish the Local for its vote, which leaves the rows in the dark for the first time in twenty years. At the end of the week the party must choose how to get into 7 North: with the superintendent, against him, or through the ridge.
setting.atmosphere: Rain most of the week, the creek high and brown, mud to the ankle on every path; cold mornings, grey noons, the sun in the hollow for an hour on Wednesday and gone. Families on the road with their furniture under tarpaulins. Men going to the drift mouth in silence, in groups of four. Lamps lit in every window all night. On Thursday night, with the ovens banked, the camp is darker than anyone alive has seen it, and you can hear the knocking under every floor on Number Two Bottom.

keyLocations.name: The Company Office
keyLocations.description: A square brick building at the foot of Silk Stocking Row with bars on the windows, a pay window at the side, a clerks' room with high desks and the tonnage sheets in green ledgers, a vault, a telephone, and at the back Superintendent Bledsoe's office: a roll-top desk, a mine map of No. 3 under glass covering one wall with 7 North hatched over in red ink, a photograph of the 1919 tipple, and a coal stove. The Ironwood shanty is across the yard, a board building with a rack of shotguns, a desk, a stove, bunks and Captain Kincaid's order book.
features: The mine map under glass: 7 North hatched in red, SEALED FIRE AREA 10-15-19, and in the northern corner, faint, a small circle marked No. 2 A.S. at the end of a cross-cut
The tonnage ledgers in the clerks' room, by check number and fortnight, back to 1911
Bledsoe's desk: locked; in the bottom drawer, under a cigar box, four brass checks, Nos. 104, 131, 230 and 251, and a yellowed telegram folded small
Kincaid's order book in the shanty, on the desk, in Kincaid's tidy hand
encounters: Vesta Spradlin standing in front of Bledsoe's desk on Monday morning, refusing to leave, and two Ironwood men who have been told to remove her and are trying to find a way that does not look like what it is
Captain Kincaid, who will see anyone who asks, offer them coffee, and explain
secrets: CLUE D2 (core, for anyone who gets into the tonnage ledgers, via Dr. Ketterly's Family Name, Frankie's nerve, a clerk with a grudge, or a night visit): check No. 230, Moses Hairston, September and October 1919, loads nearly twice the coal of any other man in the mine; two men's work on one number. Morris knows what it means at once

CLUE C2 (core, Kincaid's order book, which he will show anyone who asks, because he has nothing to hide in it): '1 Mar. Lamp house cleared for new Edison equipment. Open flame extinguished per agency regulation. Old checks discarded. Lamp man H. dismissed (seen at M.M. Sun. night).'

CLUE E7 (Bledsoe's bottom drawer, Mechanics DC 13 to open the lock, or Bledsoe himself in bd-scenario-004): the Philadelphia telegram of 17 October 1919, 'PROTECT PROPERTY. FIRE MUST BE STARVED. NO MEN TO ENTER. J.R.O.', and the four checks the Kept Light needs

keyLocations.name: The Store Ledger Room
keyLocations.description: A locked back room on the store's upper floor, shelved to the ceiling with leather-bound account ledgers, one row of shelves for each year since 1903, a high desk, a gas ring and a window onto the drift mouth. Plumley has the only key and keeps it on his watch chain. The ledgers record every scrip advance and every purchase by every family in Ottway for twenty-four years.
features: October 1919: the dead men's accounts closed out on 20 October with balances charged to their widows
A page in Plumley's own hand for 18 October 1919: seven credits of $50.00 each, 'special work, 7N', against seven check numbers
A coffin account: fourteen coffins ordered from Gale, 15 October 1919, and thirteen returned unused in November
encounters: Plumley, if he finds anyone in the room: he blusters, then sweats, then offers money, then sends for Kincaid
secrets: CLUE E2 (core, for anyone in the ledger room with an hour, Investigation DC 10 to find it faster): the seven $50 credits of 18 October 1919, with Lettie's unspent slip to match one of them. The seven check numbers belong to Lonzo Cutright, Washington Burchett, Hobart Lilly, Elmer Stacy, Arlie Sturgill, Dominic Ruggeri and Ance Kirby: the seal crew. Lonzo is the only one still in the company's employ; Hobart is in jail; Dominic is in the Local

The coffin account: fourteen ordered on 15 October, when the company still expected bodies, and thirteen returned. Somebody counted fourteen, once. One coffin was kept, and is still in the store's back room, with no name on it

keyLocations.name: Gale: the Courthouse, the Jail and the Banner
keyLocations.description: Fourteen miles down the valley, forty minutes in Della's Ford or an hour on the train, the county seat of Selden County: a sandstone courthouse with a clock tower on a square of mud and maples, the jail behind it, the Selden County Banner's office over a hardware store, a Western Union office at the depot, and a hotel where the coal companies' lawyers drink. Sheriff Boyd Sizemore's office is in the courthouse basement. Angelo Marchetti and Hobart Lilly are in the jail, charged with the murder of Lester Gaither; the grand jury sits on Saturday 16 April.
features: The county clerk's vault: inquest files by year, including the full file on the Ottway No. 3 explosion of 1919, with exhibits
The jail: four cells, a stove and a deputy reading the Banner; visiting is at the sheriff's pleasure
The Banner's morgue: bound volumes back to 1890, and a spike of letters to the editor that were never printed
The Western Union office, where the operator has instructions from the sheriff to show him any telegram addressed to a newspaper
encounters: Sheriff Boyd Sizemore, tired, courteous, owned: he will let the doctor see the prisoners (they need one; Hobart has a broken rib from his arrest), and nobody else without a reason
Ironwood men in a car outside the courthouse, writing down who goes in
secrets: CLUE E3 (core, Dr. Ketterly's Coroner practice gets the file without a check; anyone else needs a court order, a bribe or a Persuasion DC 15 with the clerk): the full inquest file holds, as an exhibit nobody read aloud, District Inspector Orval Overbey's own field notebook, which records on 16 October 'Signals reported at seal (rail, 4-2) by seal crew; Supt. advises squeeze; concur' and on 17 October 'Signals again a.m. Supt. reports No. 2 A.S. capped to starve fire on instructions of the company. Did not inspect.' It matches the public transcript's unanswered question

Hobart Lilly, visited (he will talk to Dr. Ketterly, to Della, or to anyone Della brings): he was on the seal crew. He heard them. He knows what took Gaither, because he has heard the knocking in his sleep for eight years and he knows the sound has changed. 'They knocked four and two in nineteen and nineteen and that was men. This one's been knocking four and two since March and that ain't them. That's somebody it's got.' He joined the union because of 1919. He asks the party to tell Dominic Ruggeri that he's sorry

The Banner's spike of unprinted letters, Research DC 13: a letter of 20 October 1919 from Cletus Shumate, in pencil, saying he heard men knocking in the Number Two air shaft and saw the company cap it on the 17th, which the editor marked 'No. Ottway' and spiked. (Supports E1)

keyLocations.name: Imre Halász's House on the Slate-Dump Road
keyLocations.description: A two-room company house at the end of the last row, below the slate dump, that Imre has been told to vacate by 1 May. A workbench under the window with lamps in pieces on it, a cot, a stove, a holy picture, a canvas bag that never leaves his sight, and on a nail over the bench a loop of wire with ten brass checks on it.
features: The Kept Light: a brass Wolf flame safety lamp, polished, filled, trimmed and cold, on the bench in the place of honour
Ten brass checks on a wire: nine company checks from the slate dump, and one cut from a blank and stamped by hand, E P
At night, standing in the dark round the house, just outside the window's light, grey men with lamps on their caps that are not lit
encounters: The Shades of the fourteen, ten of them, round Imre's house at night, because their checks are here (adversaries.json: Shade; fear check DC 15 to see them clearly). They do nothing, unless someone takes a check from the wire: then that man's Shade follows the check, and touches whoever carries it, cold (Cold Touch, no attack roll needed the first time, no damage, just the cold), until it is hung back up or given to someone who knew him
secrets: CLUE C1 (core, Imre, for anyone who asks about the pale square on the lamp-house wall, or about the lamp in his bag): the whole story of the Kept Light, lit on 15 October 1919, kept every shift for seven and a half years, put out by Harley Mabe with his thumb on Kincaid's order on 1 March. He does not know why he kept it. He knows that Bledsoe came to the lamp house on the night of 23 October 1919 and said 'It's quit, Imre. They've quit knocking' (CLUE A4, part)
CLUE D3 (core): the hand-stamped check, E P, for Ezell Pettaway, who had no number. Imre will give it to Morris with both hands

CLUE B4 (Imre's Old Lore, once the party have seen the Dark or its sign; or asked about the old country): 'In my village they said, never let a man go down alone, the dark is hungry. I thought it was about the roof.' (Rule 2, confirmed)

Imre's Collector clue, once this scenario: 'Fourteen checks, one light. Not one man ever taken from the board while it burned. Not one, in seven years and a half. Three weeks after, the guard.' (CLUE C5)

keyLocations.name: Mount Moriah and the Hill
keyLocations.description: The church and the school by day, and on Thursday night the Local's vote. Rev. Greer's study is a corner of the schoolroom behind a curtain, with a desk, a Bible, his commentaries and the church register in a tin box.
features: The church register: births, baptisms, marriages and burials since 1903, and a page headed October 1919 with fourteen names in Greer's hand, each with an age and a date: 23 October 1919
The memorial board under the east window, fourteen names lettered in white, Ezell Pettaway's among them
encounters: Thursday night, 14 April: the vote. Two hundred people in a church built for a hundred, by lamplight, with the Ironwood men in the road outside. The motion: that Local 5512 come out on strike on Monday unless the company opens 7 North and brings out Dewey Spradlin and the dead. The party may speak, and what they say about 1919 can carry or split the room
secrets: CLUE D4 (core): the register's memorial page, fourteen names, the date of death 23 October, not 14 October, because Greer heard about the knocking from his deacons' widows in 1919 and would not write the company's date (CLUE A4, part)

CLUE C4 (Rev. Greer, asked about Imre or the lamp): 'Imre told me once, years ago, when I asked him why he had a lamp burning in the day: it is a light for the ones not counted up. I thought it was a kindness. I didn't think it was a job.'

If the party tell the meeting what the seal crew heard in 1919, Dominic Ruggeri stands up and says he was on it. Then Lonzo Cutright, if he is there, stands up too. The room nearly breaks; Rev. Greer holds it with one sentence ('Every man here who did not hear them knock, thank God, and then sit down'). If it holds, Union Trust +2 and the vote carries; if it breaks, the Local splits along the rows and the company wins Monday

keyLocations.name: Lonzo Cutright's House
keyLocations.description: A tidy company house on Number One Bottom with a white picket fence Lonzo built himself, a garden laid out with string, a wife, Ruth, who keeps a ledger of what they are saving for the farm in Lincoln County, and on the kitchen table the fire boss's book.
features: The fire boss's book: every working place, every morning, gas readings, roof, water, initials, since 1923
A shelf of mine-rescue manuals and a framed fire boss's certificate
encounters: Ruth Cutright, who knows her husband wrote a letter in Gale on 30 March and does not know what was in it
secrets: CLUE C3 (core, the book, if Lonzo shows it or it is read): from 2 March 1927 onward, at 7 North and the main heading near it, 'lamps blue, no gas on lamp' and 'mules refuse main heading at 7N' in his hand, morning after morning; nothing of the kind in four years before
CLUE A3 (core, the book): 'knocking 7N seal' every morning 28 March to 3 April, then nothing

CLUE E5 (Lonzo's confession, when he is shown the inspector's notebook, the ledger page, or Lettie's slip, or when Dewey's nine days are counted to him aloud): everything he did in October 1919, and that he wrote the letter to the Herald. And that Bledsoe has four checks in his drawer. He will then do whatever the party ask about 7 North, including leading them in

keyLocations.name: The Lamp House at Night
keyLocations.description: After the night shift has gone in, the lamp house is Harley Mabe and the charging rack and the pale square on the wall, and Harley does not like it. Anyone can talk their way in; Garland can walk in.
features: The pale square, the fourteen nail holes, and the scorch mark
The board of the night shift's checks, a hundred and forty of them, hanging in their rows
encounters: If the Kept Light is relit here (see the Blackdamp's Rules, Rule 5, and Rites That Work), Harley Mabe will try to stop it on Kincaid's order, and then, when the lamps of the night shift far down the heading go yellow and steady for the first time since March, he will stop trying
secrets: CLUE C6 (Lettie, The Thin Place, here): a small steady flame; names said one after another in a man's voice with an accent; the strongest feeling in this room is of being counted, of a door shut against the cold. And below that, under the floor, something waiting for the door to open. It is open now

THE TEST (for any party who suspect Rule 5): hang a person's own check on a hook with a lit lamp under it and say their name, and that night that person can walk the creek path alone and the Dark will pass them by. The GM should allow it to be proven, once, at real risk

keyLocations.name: The Rows on Thursday Night
keyLocations.description: When the Local votes to strike, the company banks the coke ovens to punish it, for the first time since the 1922 strike, and the long orange street of light along the creek goes dull and dark. The rows have only their kerosene lamps. The boss row and the drift mouth keep their electric lights. And the Dark, which has been coming up only as far as the creek path and the tipple, comes into the rows.
features: Every window lit; grown-ups sitting up together in the front rooms, the children asleep in the back rooms with an adult beside them (the Dark is never shown near a child; Dread in Ottway); the knocking under every floor on Number Two Bottom
The only bright light in the bottom: the drift-mouth bulbs, the lamp house, and the street lamps on Silk Stocking Row across the creek
encounters: The Hungry Dark in the rows (adversaries.json), looking for anyone alone: a miner going to his privy, an old man asleep in his chair with the lamp gone out, an Ironwood guard posted alone at the footbridge (Elbert Toler, if he is still free, or another, Coy Dillard, 30). Make it a night of near things: the party hear the voice of the last person taken calling outside, a lamp goes blue in an empty kitchen, a door that was shut is open. Let them save one person by getting to them; the Dark uses Drink the Light and Swallowing Touch only on anyone who comes at it alone, and leaves at once when two people reach the one it wanted
Frightened Townsmen with shotguns at their doors, Jumpy
secrets: If the party save the Ironwood man at the footbridge, Kincaid hears about it by morning, and Company Suspicion -2. Kincaid does not thank anyone. He does stop calling the disappearances union work

CLUE F2 (part, for anyone who goes up to Shumate's at first light on Friday, or anyone already there with Mavis): at dawn, from the upper pasture, the darkness in the bottom of the hollow drains back up the slope toward the cap like water toward a drain, the frost ring whitens round the concrete, and the Corpse Light goes out. It goes home to the shaft. Mavis's Hunter of the Uncanny, if she has declared it her quarry, gives Rule 3 or Rule 6's 'by day it lies in the room where it began' here

synopsis: On Monday the company says squeeze and posts Kincaid's men on the seal; Vesta Spradlin stands in the superintendent's office until she is carried out; and the party have eight days. They can dig up 1919 from four directions at once: the company's own tonnage sheets and the store's ledger (two men's coal on one check, and seven $50 credits to the seal crew the day after the cap), the inquest file in Gale with the inspector's notebook ('signals reported at seal'), the jailed seal-crew man Hobart Lilly, and the Mount Moriah register with its fourteen names and its honest date. They meet Imre Halász, the old lamp man, and learn about the Kept Light, the lamp that burned under fourteen brass checks for seven and a half years and was put out three weeks before the first man was taken. On Tuesday the first families are evicted; on Thursday the Local votes, in a packed church, to strike on Monday unless 7 North is opened, and the company banks the coke ovens, and the Dark comes into the rows. On Friday the fire boss confesses and Bledsoe sends for the doctor. By Saturday the party know the whole crime and have a way to hold the Dark, if they can get the four checks out of the superintendent's drawer, and they must decide how to go into 7 North: with Bledsoe, who wants to go in first and wash the timbers; past Kincaid's guards, through the seal; or through Mavis Shumate's grandfather's coal bank and the old hole-through nobody else remembers.
hook: Monday 11 April, half past six in the morning, rain. The day shift is lined up at the lamp house and nobody is going in. Two Ironwood men stand at the drift mouth with shotguns; Captain Kincaid stands between them with a sheet of paper, reading in his quiet voice the superintendent's notice that the 7 North sealed fire area is subject to normal ground pressure and that any man interfering with the seal will be discharged and prosecuted. In the company office across the yard a small fair woman is standing in front of the superintendent's desk with her hands in her coat pockets, and has been since five, and the superintendent is sitting behind it with his hands flat on the blotter, and neither of them has said anything for twenty minutes. Somewhere a mile and a quarter inside the mountain, a man knocks on a rail. Eight days.

conclusions.conclusion: A. The fourteen lived nine days behind the seal in 1919, and Lester Gaither knocked for nine days in 1927; Dewey Spradlin has until midnight on Tuesday 19 April (Rule 4).
clues: A3: Lonzo's fire-boss book, 28 March to 3 April (Lonzo's house)
A4: the inquest's 14 October, Greer's register's 23 October, and Bledsoe's 'It's quit, Imre' (Gale, Mount Moriah, Imre's house)

conclusions.conclusion: C. The Kept Light held the Dark below ground for seven and a half years; putting it out on 1 March called it up; relit under all fourteen checks with all fourteen names, it can hold it again (Rules 1 and 5).
clues: C2: Kincaid's order book (the Ironwood shanty)
C3: the fire-boss book from 2 March (Lonzo's house)
C4: Greer's memory of Imre (Mount Moriah)
C5: Imre's Collector clue, no one taken while it burned (Imre's house)
C6: Lettie in the lamp house (the lamp house)

conclusions.conclusion: D. There were fourteen men, not thirteen; the fourteenth was Ezell Pettaway, who loaded on Moses Hairston's check No. 230 and was never on the company's books.
clues: D2: the tonnage ledgers (the company office)
D4: the Mount Moriah register (Mount Moriah)
The store's fourteenth coffin (the ledger room)

conclusions.conclusion: E. The company knew the men were alive on 16 and 17 October 1919, capped their air on Philadelphia's order, paid the seal crew to keep quiet, and listed the dead as killed instantly.
clues: E1: the cap's date, and Cletus Shumate's spiked letter (Shumate's pasture, the Banner)
E2: the store ledger's seven $50 credits (the ledger room)
E3: the inspector's field notebook (the Gale courthouse)
E7: the telegram in Bledsoe's drawer (the company office)

acts.title: Monday and Tuesday: Squeeze
acts.description: The company's answer and the camp's. The point of this act is to set the clock, show the company's reasonable face and its machinery (the notice, the guards on the seal, the evictions), and point the party at the four places 1919 is written down. Bledsoe will see anyone; Kincaid will see anyone; both will explain. Vesta will not leave the office. On Tuesday morning three families are evicted for union activity: their furniture is carried out of their houses onto the road by Ironwood men, among them, on Kincaid's order and to see what he does, Garland Hensley, and the third house is his mother's.
objectives: Hear the company's position from Bledsoe and Kincaid, and see what it costs them to hold it
Learn where 1919 is written down: the ledgers, the inquest file, the register, the fire boss's book
Meet Imre Halász and see the Kept Light
Stand with the evicted families, or not

scenes.name: The Superintendent's Office
scenes.description: Bledsoe, Vesta and two Ironwood men, at seven in the morning. Bledsoe will speak to the doctor at once, and to anyone the doctor brings. He is courteous and tired. He explains: 7 North is a sealed fire area; opening a seal over a fire, or over gas, could kill everyone in No. 3; the knocking is the mountain working, he has heard it before, and he will not risk two hundred men for a sound. He offers Vesta a widow's benefit of $300 and a job in the store and she spits on the blotter. Everything he says is the truth, about mining. Insight shows the lie is in what he does not say. If anyone mentions the air shaft, the date on the cap, or the word 'thirteen', he goes very still and asks them to leave.
scenes.readAloud: The superintendent's office smells of coal smoke and pipe tobacco, and one whole wall is the mine: a great map under glass, every entry and room and pillar of Ottway No. 3 inked in black on linen, and up in the top corner a whole section hatched over in red, as if someone had crossed it out. SEALED FIRE AREA 10-15-19. The man behind the desk is grey and neat and tired, with an engineer's square hands flat on his blotter. In front of the desk a small woman in a wet coat stands with her chin up and does not look round. 'Doctor,' says the superintendent, getting up, with real relief. 'Thank God. Perhaps you can help Mrs. Spradlin understand.'

skillChecks.success: Everything he says about seals, gas and fire is true and professional. He is not lying about mining. He is lying about the knocking, and he is lying, or leaving something out, every time the date comes up.
skillChecks.failure: A reasonable man in an unreasonable job.

skillChecks.success: He agrees to have the air behind the seal sampled by the fire boss morning and night and the readings posted, which keeps Lonzo at the seal twice a day and gives the party an ally's eyes on it.
skillChecks.failure: Company Suspicion +1. 'I think that's enough for today.'

scenes.name: Moving Day Comes Early
scenes.description: Tuesday morning, rain. Three houses on Number Two Bottom: Rad Hensley's, a Hungarian loader named Gyula Novák's, and Dovie Hensley's, because her son Rad lives with her. Ironwood men carry out bedsteads, stoves, trunks, a sewing machine and a cabinet organ and set them on the road in the mud, and the families stand by them. Neighbours come out with tarpaulins. Kincaid watches from a car. Garland is ordered to carry out his mother's things. What the party do here moves both scores: helping the families is Union Trust +1 and Company Suspicion +1; stopping it by force is a fight with six armed deputised men, which the party will lose in court even if they win it on the road. Mavis offers her pasture on the ridge for anyone who needs a place to put a tent. Della brings the Ford.
scenes.readAloud: The rain comes straight down. In front of three grey houses on Number Two Bottom there are bedsteads standing in the road, a cookstove with the pipe still on it, a trunk, a cabinet organ with a tarpaulin over it, a rocking chair, all in the mud, and families standing beside them in their coats as if they were waiting for a train. Men in khaki come out of the doorways carrying more. In the car at the end of the row, a man with steel spectacles is writing in a notebook on his knee. A tall old woman with a pipe sits in the rocking chair in the road with her hands folded and watches one of the guards, a lanky sandy-haired man, come out of her front door with her clock in his arms. He stops on the step. They look at each other.

skillChecks.success: The guards slow down, or stop, long enough for the neighbours to get every family's goods under cover and onto Della's truck; nothing is broken. Union Trust +1.
skillChecks.failure: It goes on, and something is broken: the organ, dropped in the road. The camp remembers who stood and watched.

skillChecks.success: (On Kincaid.) He is not watching the families. He is watching Garland Hensley, and writing.

scenes.name: The Lamp Man
scenes.description: Imre Halász, at his bench, with the Kept Light. Anyone who asks about the pale square, or who is sent by Lettie (who brings him soup) or Greer, or who sees grey men standing round his house at night, will be let in and given coffee and told, in exact and careful detail, about the lamp. He does not know why he kept it. He knows when. Morris, if present, is given Ezell's check with both hands. At night, the Shades stand round the house in the rain, ten of them, because ten checks are here; through the window, if anyone is brave enough to look, you can see that each one is a man in pit clothes with his lamp unlit, and that they are looking at the wire on the nail.
scenes.readAloud: The old man sets the lamp on the bench between you as carefully as if it were full of something that might spill. It is brass, the old kind, a little tower of gauze and glass with a hook on top, polished until it shines like a church thing. It is cold. 'Seven years and a half,' he says. 'Every shift, I fill. Every Sunday, I come in, I fill. Christmas, I fill. The strike of twenty-two, no work, I come in, I fill. I hang it here,' he lifts his hand, 'under the board. Fourteen checks. Thirteen the company gives, one I make.' He touches the wire on the nail. 'They are not counted up. A lamp man counts them down, counts them up. These I never count up. So I keep a light.' He looks at the lamp. 'Then the first of March the young man puts it out. With his thumb.' He shows you, pinching his own finger and thumb together. 'Pff.'

skillChecks.success: (Or an Occultist's Old Lore.) A light kept for the dead, kept long enough, is a promise, and a promise kept long enough holds things. When it is broken, what it held is let go.
skillChecks.failure: An old man's grief, and a very beautiful lamp.

skillChecks.success: (At night, at the window.) They are standing in the rain looking at the checks, that is all. They want them. They are not coming in.
skillChecks.failure: Ten men are standing in the dark in the rain round the house, with their lamps out, and they are dead, and they are looking at you because you are standing next to their names. Gain 1 Dread.

encounters: The eviction: six Ironwood men (Night Watchman), Captain Kincaid (Deputy Sheriff stats, 30 HP) in the car; a fight here is possible and a terrible idea
The Shades at Imre's house (adversaries.json: Shade x10; they do not attack unless someone tries to take or destroy the checks, and a line of salt keeps them out of the house)

acts.title: Wednesday and Thursday: The Books and the Vote
acts.description: The party dig up 1919 and bring it to the camp. The point of this act is to let the party assemble the crime from three or four independent records, decide who to tell, and put it before the Local on Thursday night, where it can unite the camp or split it. Wednesday is the day for Gale: Della drives, the Ford breaks down twice, the courthouse is a long morning, the jail an afternoon, the Banner an hour. Wednesday night or Thursday morning is for the ledger room and the tonnage sheets, which need either Dr. Ketterly's name, Garland's badge, a bribe to a clerk, or a break-in. Thursday night is the vote, and after it the ovens are banked and the Dark comes into the rows.
objectives: Find the inspector's notebook in the Gale inquest file, and talk to Hobart Lilly
Find the seven $50 credits in the store ledger and Moses Hairston's double tonnage in the company's books
Read the Mount Moriah register, and learn what Imre told Greer
Decide what to tell the Local, and survive the night the ovens go dark

scenes.name: The Inquest File
scenes.description: The county clerk's vault in the courthouse basement. Dr. Ketterly asks as deputy coroner and gets the file in ten minutes; anyone else needs the Family Name, a court order, a dollar, or a long argument. The file is thick: the transcript, the company's list of thirteen, a plan of 7 North, the inspector's formal report, and in an envelope marked Exhibit F, never read aloud, District Inspector Overbey's own pocket field notebook. Its pages for 16 and 17 October are the clue. A clerk who remembers 1919 says Overbey resigned the next spring and went to Ohio.
scenes.readAloud: The notebook is small and black and has been wet once, and the pages have dried rippled. A neat, slanting, tired hand, pencil. 'Thurs. 16th. Ottway No. 3, 7N seals, both stoppings 2/3 complete. Signals reported at seal (rail, 4-2) by seal crew, 2.15 p.m. Supt. B. advises squeeze over fire; concur.' Under it, in the same hand, a little later, pressed harder: 'Asked Supt. whether rescue possible. Supt. says fire between seal and face, no.' Then, Friday: 'Fri. 17th. Signals again reported a.m. Supt. reports No. 2 A.S. capped this morning to starve fire, on instructions of the company. Did not inspect.' The last three words are underlined twice.

skillChecks.success: Set against the public transcript: the inquest heard none of this. Overbey's formal report says the men 'perished at once in the explosion'. He wrote that a month after he wrote this.
You make yourself read it the way Frankie or the doctor would read it: as evidence, dated and signed.
skillChecks.failure: The truth of it: they knew. They heard them, and wrote it down, and capped the air, and went home. Gain 1 Dread.

scenes.name: The Ledger Room
scenes.description: At night, or in daylight with a good story. Plumley keeps the key on his watch chain; there is a second key in the scrip clerk's drawer. The ledger for 1919 has the seven credits and the coffin account; the company office's tonnage sheets (across the yard, a separate job) have check No. 230. If Plumley catches anyone, he can be bought ($50, which is a fine joke), frightened (he is terrified of Kincaid finding out how much Plumley knows), or he sends for Kincaid, which is Company Suspicion +2 and a night in the Ironwood shanty for whoever was caught.
scenes.readAloud: The ledger for 1919 is as big as a gravestone and twice as heavy. October. A page of ordinary things, flour, lard, overalls, powder, and then, in a different, more careful hand, seven lines in a row, each against a check number: '18 Oct. Special work, 7N. Cr. 50.00.' Fifty dollars was two months' wages in 1919. A little further on, under 15 October, an order to an undertaker in Gale: fourteen coffins, plain pine, and under it, in November: '13 returned, credit.'

skillChecks.success: In and out without Plumley or the Ironwood night man knowing; take the page, or Frankie's photograph of it.
skillChecks.failure: A light comes on downstairs. You have one round to decide whether to run, hide or explain.

skillChecks.success: The seven check numbers are the seal crew: Cutright, Burchett, Lilly, Stacy, Sturgill, Ruggeri, Kirby. Two still in Ottway; one in jail.

scenes.name: The Vote
scenes.description: Thursday night at Mount Moriah: two hundred people, the windows sacked, the Ironwood men in the road. The motion to strike on Monday unless the company opens 7 North. The party may speak. If they lay out 1919, the seal-crew men stand up, one, then two (see Mount Moriah's secrets), and the room either holds or breaks. Rev. Greer is the hinge. If it holds, the vote carries by a show of hands in which Black, white and Hungarian hands go up together and Union Trust +2; if it breaks, the Local splits, the vote fails, and Company Suspicion +1 because Kincaid learns who spoke. Either way, at ten o'clock word comes that the company has banked the coke ovens, and the long orange light along the creek is going out.
scenes.readAloud: There is no room to sit. People stand in the aisles and along the walls and in the open doorway, and the stove is roaring and the windows are running with steam behind their feed sacks, and the lantern on the pulpit shakes every time someone stamps. A young man with a red face stands at the front with a sheet of paper and reads the motion in his judge's voice, and stops. In the silence a man at the back stands up. He is sixty, white-haired, an Italian loader with a face like a walnut. 'Dominic Ruggeri,' he says. 'Check number two-fifty-eight. I was on that crew. I want to say it before somebody else does.' Nobody breathes. Then, from the side aisle, a spare grey man with a safety lamp on his belt gets up too.

skillChecks.success: What you say lets the room hear that the men who laid the block were ordered, lied to and paid, and that the men who gave the orders are still in the office. The room holds. Union Trust +2.
skillChecks.failure: The room hears that men in it heard the fourteen knock and kept working. It goes ugly. Rev. Greer holds it from breaking into a fight, but the Local splits along the rows tonight.

skillChecks.success: Rad Hensley is looking at his brother Garland, if Garland is here. If Garland stands up now and says what he knows about 25 March, the room will forgive a great deal.

scenes.name: The Night the Ovens Went Dark
scenes.description: From ten on Thursday night until dawn, the rows have no light but their own. The Dark comes up out of the drift mouth and down into Number Two Bottom and along the creek and up toward the Hill. The party, coming home from Mount Moriah in a group, are safe, and should know it; the question is who else is alone. Run it as a sequence of near things: the voice of the last person taken calling outside a house; a lamp guttering blue in an empty kitchen; a privy door swinging open; an Ironwood guard posted alone at the footbridge who cannot leave his post. The party can save one or two people by getting to them before it does. Whoever they cannot reach, or do not try to, is taken, and their nine days begin.
scenes.readAloud: The ovens go out one by one along the creek, the orange in their mouths going red and then brown and then nothing, and with each one the dark comes a little closer up the bottom, until the only lights in Ottway are the windows of the rows, small and yellow and far apart, and across the creek the street lamps of Silk Stocking Row, white and steady, like a different town. In the houses around you, people are sitting up together in their front rooms with every lamp lit, and you can hear, if you stand still in the road, the knocking under every floor on Number Two Bottom at once. And then, from down by the footbridge, a young man's voice you know calls out, 'Hello? Is somebody there? I can't see.'

skillChecks.success: It is using his voice. You know the rule. You go together.
skillChecks.failure: Dewey is out there, alone, in the dark, calling, and he is behind the seal a mile inside the mountain. Gain 1 Dread.

skillChecks.success: The guard at the footbridge: alone, his flashlight flickering, backing up the bridge away from something on the far bank that his light does not reach. You have about a round.
skillChecks.failure: A light at the footbridge, flickering. Then not.

encounters: The Hungry Dark in the rows on Thursday night (adversaries.json: 60 HP, AC 13, resists ordinary weapons; Drink the Light recharge 5-6; it avoids anyone in company, and anything bright; reduced to 0 it breaks apart until the next night)
Frightened Townsmen at their doors with shotguns, Jumpy
Plumley and the Ironwood night man at the store, if the ledger room goes wrong (Night Watchman)

acts.title: Friday and Saturday: Which Way In
acts.description: The truth assembled, the camp at the edge, and the choice. The point of this act is to let the party put the crime together, get the fire boss's confession and a guide, decide whether to relight the Kept Light, and choose a route into 7 North with three days left on Dewey's clock. On Friday morning Lonzo Cutright comes to whoever has been kindest to him. On Friday afternoon Bledsoe sends for Dr. Ketterly. On Saturday the Gale grand jury hears the Gaither case.
objectives: Get Lonzo Cutright's confession, his map and his help
Get the four checks out of Bledsoe's drawer, by persuasion, theft or a new stamp from someone who knew the men, and decide whether to relight the Kept Light
Choose the way into 7 North: with Bledsoe through the seal, against Kincaid through the seal, or through the Shumate hole-through

scenes.name: The Fire Boss
scenes.description: Lonzo, at Lettie's kitchen table at five on Friday morning, after his round, with his book and his map. If he has been shown the inspector's notebook, the ledger page, or Wash's slip, or if someone counts Dewey's days to him aloud, he confesses everything (CLUE E5): the knocking on the 16th, Bledsoe's 'squeeze', the 17th, the telegram, the fifty dollars, the letter to the Herald. Then he unfolds his 1919 map of 7 North on the oilcloth and shows them the barricade room at the foot of the Number Two air shaft, the two seals, and, in pencil, a thing that is not on the company's map: the old Shumate hole-through.
scenes.readAloud: He unfolds the map on Lettie's oilcloth as if it might tear, and it might: it has been folded into his pocket every day for eight years. Entries, rooms, pillars, in faded blue. He puts his finger on a little circle in the top corner. 'Number Two. They'd have gone there for the air. Lafe Combs would have took them there; he knew the shaft. Here's the seals. Mile and a quarter between.' He moves his finger, slowly, past the seals and round the edge of the sheet, to a pencil line that goes off the paper. 'And here's the old Shumate country bank. Company holed through into it in sixteen, robbing pillars, and bricked it up again. It ain't on the seal plan. Nobody'd think of it but Mavis and me.' He takes his finger off the map. 'I'll go. Whichever way. I'll go first. I always go first.'

skillChecks.success: He means it, all of it, and he has not slept. He wants to go in first because going in first is the only thing he knows how to do that might make it right.
skillChecks.failure: A tired man with a map.

skillChecks.success: (Reading the map with him.) Through the seal: an hour by man-trip, four hours to break a stopping, firedamp to test first, Kincaid's guards. Through the hole-through: three hours crawling, a flooded dip, and nobody knows you're there.

scenes.name: The Superintendent Sends for the Doctor
scenes.description: Friday afternoon. Bledsoe, alone, in his office, with the door shut. He has heard about the vote, the ledger room and the inspector's notebook, and he knows his week is over. He offers Dr. Ketterly, and anyone the doctor trusts, a deal: on Saturday night, with Lonzo and four company men, he will break the left-hand seal himself and go in for Dewey, if the doctor will come as medical officer and the party will come with him and say nothing about anything else they find. What he means to do, which Insight DC 15 shows, is reach the barricade room first and wash the timbers. If he is told plainly that the party know, he does not deny it. He sits for a long time. Then he opens the bottom drawer and puts the four checks on the blotter, and keeps his hand on the telegram.
scenes.readAloud: He does not get up this time. He sits with his hands flat on the blotter and the red-hatched corner of the map behind his head, and he looks older than he did on Monday by about ten years. 'I was the mine foreman,' he says. 'I was forty-eight. I'd been in the mines since I was fourteen. I listened to that rail for an hour, Doctor. I told myself it was squeeze. Do you know, I nearly believed it? For a whole day.' He looks at the map. 'Then the telegram. I could have gone up that ridge and stood on the shaft and not let them pour. I had the authority. I had the men. I didn't.' He opens the bottom drawer, slowly, and takes out four brass checks and puts them on the blotter in a row. 'I couldn't throw these away,' he says. 'Isn't that a funny thing.'

skillChecks.success: He gives up the checks, and, if pressed, agrees to go in the party's way and not his own: he will open the seal for them on Saturday night and keep Kincaid's men off it, and ruin himself.
skillChecks.failure: He keeps the checks, and the telegram, and offers his deal again, and you can see him decide that you are not to be trusted.

skillChecks.success: He wants to be stopped. He has wanted it for eight years. He is not brave enough to stop himself.
skillChecks.failure: A broken man, or a clever one.

encounters: Kincaid's men posted on the seal, four on each shift, and on the drift mouth (Night Watchman)
If the Kept Light is relit in the lamp house: Harley Mabe and the night Ironwood man try to stop it on Kincaid's standing order, until they see what it does
The Gale grand jury on Saturday: without a body, it holds Angelo and Hobart over to the June term; the party cannot change that until they bring out Lester Gaither

npcsInvolved.name: Superintendent Elwood Bledsoe, 56
npcsInvolved.role: The man who capped the shaft
npcsInvolved.description: Courteous, competent and hollowed out. This week he goes from 'squeeze' to an offer to break his own seal. He can be the party's worst enemy in bd-scenario-003 or its strangest ally.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To reach the barricade room first and wash the timbers; underneath that, to be stopped.

npcsInvolved.name: Captain Arliss Kincaid, 44
npcsInvolved.description: Neat, quiet, reasonable. This week he runs the evictions, posts the seal, banks the ovens on the company's order, and watches Garland. He loses a man on Thursday night if the party do not save him.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The Local broken by Monday; nobody into 7 North before the company crew; his men alive, which is new.

npcsInvolved.name: Vinton Plumley, 50
npcsInvolved.role: Store manager and keeper of the ledgers
npcsInvolved.description: Frightened, blustering, venal, and the man who wrote the seven credits with his own pen.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Not to be the man Kincaid blames.

npcsInvolved.name: Sheriff Boyd Sizemore, 60
npcsInvolved.description: Heavy, slow, polite, honest about being owned. He will let the doctor see the prisoners and will tell anyone who asks that he would release them tomorrow if someone gave him a body.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be left alone until the November election.

npcsInvolved.name: Hobart Lilly, 47
npcsInvolved.description: A big, slow, gentle loader with a broken rib and a Bible, who heard the fourteen knock and laid block anyway and has heard it in his sleep ever since.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be forgiven by Dominic Ruggeri, and to see the fourteen brought out.

npcsInvolved.name: Angelo Marchetti, 41
npcsInvolved.description: A short, quick, funny Calabrian loader who argued with Lester Gaither about a short weight and has been in jail three weeks for it.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get out and to make sure Della does not do anything he would have to bail her out for.

npcsInvolved.name: Dominic Ruggeri, 60
npcsInvolved.description: A white-haired Piedmontese loader, a widower who sings bass in the choir at St. Stephen's, who stands up at the vote.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To say it aloud before he dies.

npcsInvolved.name: Ruth Cutright, 46
npcsInvolved.description: A small precise woman with a ledger of savings and a husband who has not slept since March.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The farm in Lincoln County, and Lonzo alive to farm it.

npcsInvolved.name: Coy Dillard, 30
npcsInvolved.role: Ironwood guard at the footbridge on Thursday night
npcsInvolved.description: A former railroad brakeman, sardonic and brave and alone at his post because Kincaid will not let a post go unmanned.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep his job; not to be taken.

rewards.money: Frankie's editor wires $50 and the words 'HOLD FOR PROOF' when she sends him the inspector's notebook. The Local cannot pay, but its members feed the party all week, find them dry beds, and lend them anything they ask for: tools, rope, lamps, a mule. Plumley's $50 bribe, if taken, is in scrip.
items: Ten brass checks and the Kept Light, from Imre; four more from Bledsoe's drawer, if got
Ezell Pettaway's hand-stamped check, given to Morris
A photograph or copy of Inspector Overbey's field notebook, pages for 16 and 17 October 1919
The store ledger page of 18 October 1919, or Frankie's photograph of it
Lonzo Cutright's 1919 map of 7 North, with the Shumate hole-through in pencil
The Philadelphia telegram, if Bledsoe lets go of it

twists: Bledsoe's four checks include No. 230, Moses Hairston's: the check Ezell Pettaway loaded on. Bledsoe has known for eight years that there were two men on it.

If the party relight the Kept Light with all fourteen checks and names, the Dark is held in 7 North: no one else is taken on the surface, the night shift's lamps burn steady for the first time since March, and the camp notices. But it means the Dark is in 7 North by night as well as by day when the party go in.

Kincaid knew about the four checks in Bledsoe's drawer, because he saw Bledsoe take them out of the bucket. He has said nothing, because it is the kind of thing that can be useful about a superintendent.
The one coffin the store kept in 1919, with no name on it, was kept by Plumley's order on a note from Bledsoe: 'Hold one. Pettaway.' Bledsoe knew the name.
dmTips: This scenario is the investigation, and it is a lot of material. Every core clue is found by anyone who looks in the right place; the party do not need all of it. The crime (E) needs any two of the cap, the ledger, the notebook and Lonzo; the fourteenth name (D) needs any two of the tonnage sheets, Imre's check and the register; the Kept Light (C) needs Imre and one more.

Keep the clock visible. Dewey has until midnight on Tuesday. If the party spend Wednesday in Gale and Thursday in the ledger room and Friday arguing, they go in on Saturday or Sunday, which is fine; if they are still talking on Monday, Lonzo goes in alone through the hole-through, and the party must follow him or let him go.

The vote is the emotional centre. Let the seal-crew men be heard. The point is not that they were villains; it is that they were ordered, lied to, frightened for their jobs and paid, and that the men who did the ordering are still in the office. Rev. Greer can say that if no player does.
The company is not a monolith this week: Bledsoe breaks, Kincaid loses a man and changes his mind about who is taking them, Plumley is terrified. Let the party see cracks they can use.
Thursday night is a horror set piece in which the party are safe if they stay together and the question is who else they can reach. Reward running toward the voice in pairs; never punish it.
Relighting the Kept Light is a real choice with a cost. It saves lives on the surface tonight and makes 7 North more dangerous. Do not tell the players which is right.
